text.p: The Italian cabinet on Thursday approved a corrective budget needed to keep the country on track to enter the single European currency.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi told reporters the mini-budget would include 15.5 trillion lire ($9.2 billion) of deficit cuts needed to plug a hole in Italy's state accounts and meet the terms of the Maastricht Treaty. ($ = 1677 Italian Lire)
"The government has approved a corrective budget that will enable us to meet the parameters," Prodi told a news conference after the cabinet had approved the package.

Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi, detailing the measures, said the mini-budget would raise around six trillion lire this year by calling on companies to pay taxes ahead of time on severance payment funds.
A further six trillion lire would be raised next year by the same measure which would only affect firms with more than 15 employees, Ciampi said.

Ciampi said 2.6 trillion lire would be raised this year by delaying payment of severance handouts to state workers who took early retirement. Some 1.3 trillion lire would be saved by cutting back ministerial budgets over the last nine months of the year and four trillion lire would come from fiscal measures.
